paragraphs: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Elam: they told him in a dream, ‘Rejoice in your heart, for your dwelling and Nannas the butcher’s dwelling in the Garden of Eden, and your portion and his portion, are equal.’ When Rabbi Yehoshua awoke, he thought to himself: ‘Woe to me! Since the day I was born, I have always feared my Maker and labored only in Torah. I have not walked four cubits without tzitzit and tefillin, and I had eighty students. Now my deeds and Torah are weighed equally with those of the butcher!’ He sent word to his students: ‘Know that I shall not enter the study house until I see who this man is, what his deeds are, and how he is my companion in the Garden of Eden.’ He immediately went with his students from town to town, asking by the man’s name and his father’s name, until he reached his town. Upon entering he immediately asked: ‘Where is Nannas the butcher?’ They told him: ‘Why do you seek him? You are pious and righteous, yet you ask about a man like him?’ He asked: ‘What are his deeds?’ They replied: ‘Our lord, ask nothing about him until you see him at once.’ They sent for him, telling him: ‘Rabbi Yehoshua ben Elam asks for you.’ Nannas replied: ‘Who am I, and who are my fathers in Israel, that Rabbi Yehoshua should ask for me?’ They told him: ‘Rise and come with us.’ He thought that everything they had told him was false and said: ‘I shall not go with you, for you are making fun of me.’ They immediately returned to Rabbi Yehoshua and told him: ‘You are Israel’s light, the light of our eyes, the crown of our heads. How can you send us for him? He refused to come with us!’ He told them: ‘Know that I shall not sit until I see him.’ Rabbi Yehoshua himself went to Nannas the butcher. Nannas fell upon his face before Rabbi Yehoshua and said: ‘How is today different from other days, that Israel’s crown comes before his servant?’ He replied: ‘I have something to speak about with you.’ He said: ‘Speak.’ He asked: ‘What are your deeds, and what is your occupation?’ He replied: ‘My lord, I am a butcher. I have an elderly father and mother who cannot stand on their feet. Every day I dress them, feed them, and wash them with my own hands.’ Rabbi Yehoshua immediately stood and kissed him on his head, telling him: ‘My son, happy are you, and happy your lot! How good and pleasant it is! Happy is my portion, that I have merited to be your companion in the Garden of Eden’ (a small book of tales, under ‘Honor your father’).
